correctness.rationale: Four proof equivalences verified: bipartite edge/line graph; dominating iff no isolated row or column (union); line graph perfect matching iff every edge-component has even cardinality (constructive spanning-tree pairing); connected graph exponential formula and parity projection yielding the square-root expression. The isolated-vertex inclusion-exclusion and min formula include m=n=1 and m=1 boundaries. Independent brute-force and formal coefficient procedures agree for all sixteen boards through four by four; finite check corroborates, not proves, general statement.

evidence: An arbitrary rook-cell subset is an edge subset of \(K_{m,n}\), and the induced rook graph is its line graph. The nearest full primary paper (Brešar–Henning–Rall 2005, Sec. 3) studies paired-domination bounds and not edge-parity enumeration.

value.rationale: The complete size distribution of paired-dominating sets across every rectangular rook graph is a mathematically natural invariant, strictly finer than its minimum. The result gives a structural all-subset classification and a directly coefficient-computable bivariate series via edge-component parity, with a sharp scalar minimum as a consequence. It is not merely a finite census or a relabeled textbook deduction.
